Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Setup 3 Game Play 4 Fugitive First Turn 5 Creating Hideouts 5.1 Example 5.2 Sprinting 5.2.1 Example 6 Fugitive Normal Turn 7 Marshal First Turn 8 Uncovering Hideouts 8.1 Single Guess 8.2 Multiple Guesses 9 Marshal Normal Turn 10 Game End 10.1 Manhunt 10.1.1 Highest Revealed Hideout is Less Than 30 10.1.2 Highest Revealed Hideout is 30 or Higher 11 Strategies and Tips 11.1 Fugitive Strategy 11.2 Marshal Strategy 12 Winning Through Deduction Overview Fugitive is a quick two-player game where one player is the Fugitive moving from hideout to hideout along an escape route, while the other player is the Marshal trying to catch the Fugitive before they escape. The deck is composed of 43 cards numbered 0–42 , each representing a possible hideout. If the Fugitive successfully plays Hideout #42 , they have escaped and win the game. If the Marshal uncovers every one of the Fugitive's hideouts before then, the Marshal wins. Setup Place the 0 card face up in the center row as the Fugitive's starting location. The Fugitive begins the game with: Cards 1 , 2 , 3 , and 42 . Separate the remaining cards into three draw decks: Deck 1: Cards 4–14 The Fugitive draws 3 cards from this deck. Deck 2: Cards 15–28 The Fugitive draws 2 cards from this deck. Deck 3: Cards 29–41 No cards are drawn from this deck during setup. Shuffle each deck separately and place them face down. The Marshal begins the game with no cards . Game Play Players alternate turns throughout the game. During the Fugitive's turn, they may extend their escape route by creating a new hidden hideout to the right. During the Marshal's turn, they attempt to uncover those hidden hideouts through deduction and guessing. Fugitive First Turn On the first turn of the game, the Fugitive establishes two hideouts. Each hideout is placed face down in the center row to the right of the previous hideout (starting with the 0 card). Creating Hideouts Each newly played hideout must satisfy the following rules: It must have a higher number than the previous hideout. It may normally increase by only 1, 2, or 3 . Example If the previous hideout is 4 , the next hideout may only be: 5 , 6 or 7 The Fugitive may never move backward by playing a lower-numbered hideout. Sprinting To move farther than three spaces, the Fugitive may Sprint . When Sprinting, additional cards are placed face down below the new hideout. Each Sprint card contributes either +1 or +2 (number of foot steps shown in the top right hand corner). The combined Sprint value must make up the extra distance beyond the normal movement of three spaces. Example Previous hideout: 4 Desired hideout: 10 Normally the Fugitive could only move to 7 . Since 10 is three spaces farther, Sprint cards totaling at least +3 must be placed beneath the 10 hideout. The Fugitive may always overpay for a Sprint by placing more Sprint value than required, even if no Sprint movement is actually needed. After placing the initial two hideouts, the Fugitive's first turn ends. Fugitive Normal Turn At the start of each turn after the first, the Fugitive draws one card from any of the three draw decks and adds it to their hand. The Fugitive may then: Establish one new hideout by placing a card face down to the right of their most recent hideout. Sprint to the new hideout by placing Sprint cards underneath it, following the normal Sprint rules. The Fugitive is not required to establish a new hideout each turn. Instead, they may simply announce "Pass" . The Fugitive may look at any of their own face-down Hideout and Sprint cards at any time during the game. Marshal First Turn On the firs

[Rating: 5/10] Owned, then sold.  Then the new packaging and KS brought me back in.  Still the same game play, but I missed it's cute art and potential.

[Rating: 5/10] Playing as the Marshal significantly more fun than Fugitive, for me. Feels like the Fugitive is basically setting up the puzzle for the Marshal, otherwise the bluffing and hand management isn't tooooo interesting. Shift cards aren't particularly fun, and a whole Shift game series is way too long (best of 3 took 1h, so many better games you can play in that same time).  Playing as Marshal: 6/10 Playing as Fugitive: 4/10

[Rating: 5/10] This was quite of a letdown as we played during vacation. Production quality is outstanding however the game alas wasn't that much fun. Our main issues were that the Marshall gameplay boils down very fast to basically playing Battleship. Whereas the Fugitive is most of the time just a runaway leader. All deduction feels like just a lucky guess the more the game unfolds and there was quite a bit of boredom and frustration involved for such a small and light game.

[Rating: 6/10] Fugitive is a very stripped down hidden movement game.  I generally like mechanically pure games, but this feels too much like a guessing game and nothing more.  There is deduction to do as the marshal, but it's very simple and usually just narrows your options down to 2 or 3 guesses.  I suppose most other hidden movement games come down to making luck-based guesses, but other games feel more psychological because the hider has more agency.  Here they have to react at least somewhat to the cards drawn.  Fugitive still has a fun factor, it's quick, and I wouldn't turn down a game if suggested.

[Rating: 6/10] It's a fair game with a good production.  Not enough staying power for me. I sold it after few plays
